name: Ireland
dek: Dublin Airport's 1991–2020 normal. Not a national average. The west coast is a different file.
paragraphs: The table is Dublin Airport, filename 03969, and the header prints the number as 3969. The height in the file is 71 m. Casement Aerodrome is another station in the Irish submission and was not averaged with the airport. Cork, Shannon, Belmullet, Malin Head, and Valentia are in the same submission and are not this table.

The airport's average highs stay in single digits in winter and reach the high teens in July. Rain is in every month. CDC's Ireland page is more specific about water than the pages for the other countries in this batch, and the sheet quotes it instead of turning it into a yes. The tipping line is Ireland.com's taxi page only. That page does not give a restaurant percentage.

climate.caption: Reference station: Dublin Airport, WMO 03969. The file prints the number as 3969. Not a national average.
climate.note: World Meteorological Organization 1991–2020 climatological standard normals, distributed by NOAA NCEI. Monthly values are copied as printed, with leading spaces removed. The header field prints 3969. The filename uses 03969. Those are the same station. Casement Aerodrome is a separate file and was not averaged with this one.

plugs.label: Plugs and voltage
plugs.detail: The IEC world-plugs list, in the copy archived on 16 August 2026, shows Ireland at the voltage, frequency, and plug types in the figure. A direct download of the live page on 15 November 2026 did not return the list. The archive is the copy that was read.

driving.label: Driving side
driving.detail: Regulation 9 of the Road Traffic (Traffic and Parking) Regulations, 1997 (S.I. No. 182 of 1997) says that, save where the regulations otherwise require, a vehicle shall be driven on the left hand side of the roadway so as to allow approaching traffic to pass on the right and overtaking traffic to overtake on the right, without danger or inconvenience. The interpretation rule in the same instrument says left and right are determined by facing the direction of traffic flow.
driving.sourceTitle: S.I. No. 182/1997, regulation 9, Irish Statute Book

tipping.label: Tipping
tipping.value: Not essential for taxis; at least 10–15% if you tip
tipping.detail: Ireland.com's taxi page, which shows a last-updated date of 14 November 2023, says it is not essential to tip a taxi driver in Ireland, and that if you choose to tip, go for at least 10–15% of the fare. The page is about taxis. It does not state a restaurant percentage, so none is printed.

water.label: Tap water
water.detail: CDC's traveler page for Ireland, last reviewed 25 August 2026, says food and water standards in Ireland are similar to those in the United States, and that most travelers do not need to take special food or water precautions beyond what they normally do at home. It also says water-quality issues with unregulated drinking-water sources such as private wells have been reported in rural areas, and that travelers in rural or remote areas should ask about the source and take special precautions if the water is unregulated or unknown. This page does not turn that into a yes for every tap.

currency.label: Currency
currency.detail: ISO 4217 lists the currency name Euro and the code EUR for Ireland.

timeZone.label: Time zone
timeZone.detail: IANA's zone.tab and zone1970.tab each give Ireland one row, Europe/Dublin. There is no second Irish zone in either file.

entry.label: Official entry requirements
entry.note: The immigration service's page for a visit. We do not restate a visa rule.

bestTime.intro: Month by month for Dublin, from the Dublin Airport table above and two Met Éireann pages. Met Éireann says May and June are Ireland's sunniest months, with 5 to 6.5 hours of sunshine a day over most of the country, and December the dullest, with about 1 hour a day in the north to almost 2 in the extreme southeast. Its temperature page says inland air temperatures normally reach 18 to 20 °C on summer days and about 8 °C in winter. The airport is on the east coast; the west and the uplands are wetter.
